Not quite. The evidence supports a narrower statement: no tree-cover loss event of 0.5 ha or more was detected within the asset between 2021 and 2025, with valid observations covering the whole asset.

That isn't the same as "unchanged." Smaller changes (under 0.5 ha), changes at edges, or changes narrower than the 30 m pixels could be missed. The data also only detect stand-replacing loss, so it says nothing about gains or gradual degradation.

For context, the 2020 reference map shows 43.3 ha of forest (11.55% of the 374.8 ha asset).

This also isn't a regulatory finding. It doesn't establish EUDR compliance or deforestation-free status, and it covers only 2021–2025.
